From: Samir Rao <samir@horizen.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: where are requests executed and can you confirm deletion SLAs?

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo earlier — the product looks promising. Our security team is doing a short checklist before we move to an internal POC. Could you confirm: 

- Which regions/processors handle inference requests for the hosted API (primary + failover)?
- Which subprocessors (cloud providers, analytics, logging) see request payloads or logs?
- Are there cross-border transfers we should be aware of (especially EU->US or vice versa)?
- Deletion SLA: if a user requests deletion, what is the measurable timeline and are there proven erasure steps for caches/KV stores?

We don't need deep architectural diagrams yet — just a concise Q&A and any artifacts (one-pager or roster) you can share for our InfoSec team. If easier, loop whoever owns the residency/subprocessors docs.

Best,
Samir
Director of Security
Horizen Health
[Horizen Health (external)]

From: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where are requests executed and can you confirm deletion SLAs?

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the note and the concise list. I've put together a short summary below and attached a factsheet that should help your InfoSec reviewers. Karthik is cc'd for the low-level mapping and subprocessor roster if you want finer granularity.

High-level answers (hosted API):
- Primary execution: US (us-east-1) by default for US customers; EU workloads can be pinned to eu-west-1 on request.
- Failover/replication: automated multi-region failover may route requests to nearest healthy region (us-east-1 <-> us-west-2, eu-west-1 fallback in EU).
- Subprocessors that process inference requests or transiently hold KV/cache data: AWS (EC2, S3), GCP (Cloud Storage for logs/archives when customer opts in), and our edge partner (EdgeOps) in APAC for low-latency edge serving.
- Cross-border transfers: by default US-hosted requests remain in US; if the customer enables multi-region or uses global routing, request routing can cross borders (we document these scenarios).
- Deletion SLA: Primary path (hosted API) — user-triggered deletion request handled within 72 hours for customer-visible data; full KV/cache purge and third-party retention reconciliation completed within 30 days. For dedicated/private deployments we can contract different timelines.

Attachments: Residency_Factsheet.pdf (summary) and a subprocessor roster are included; Karthik will attach the detailed roster workbook and SOC2 evidence summary on the next message.

Next steps: if your team wants a quick walkthrough of the roster and export-control notes, we can schedule a 30-minute call this week.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where are requests executed and can you confirm deletion SLAs?

Samir / Grace — adding the more granular breakdown K wanted. I'll keep this succinct and call out the items InfoSec usually asks for.

1) Regions & routing behavior
- Hosted API default: us-east-1 (primary). EU-only tenancy can be configured to keep execution in eu-west-1; this is a per-account setting and we document the pinning process.
- Failover: health-based routing can direct traffic to us-west-2 or eu-west-1 depending on proximity and region config.
- Private or Dedicated: can be deployed inside a customer VPC/region to guarantee locality.

2) Subprocessors that may see payloads / transient data
- AWS (EC2, ELB, S3) — primary runtime and object storage for model artifacts and optional logs.
- Google Cloud (GCS, Pub/Sub) — used for optional log ingestion, analytics pipelines, and long-term archives when customers opt in.
- EdgeOps (partner) — provides edge proxying/short-term cache in APAC; only used when edge routing is enabled for latency-sensitive customers.
- PagerHound (error paging) and OpsLedger (SaaS billing & usage) — these services see metadata and alerts but not full request bodies by default.

3) Cross-border transfer controls
- We maintain documentation of every processing path. If you require EU -> EU-only processing we can lock routing and provide contractual guarantees (Data Processing Amendment + region pin).
- For global redundancy or cross-region failover we provide clear notices in the DPA and log exports so you can audit when/where requests moved.

4) Deletion & evidence of erasure
- Customer-visible deletion: 72 hours for user-surface artifacts (indexes, embeddings).
- Backend purge: KV cache evictions and scheduled secure wipe of transient caches within 30 days.
- Logs & backups: retained per account policy; default log retention 90 days, automated deletion per account policy thereafter. For compliance reviews we can produce an evidence package showing deletion timestamps and affected object IDs.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_2027.xlsx; redwood-soc2-summary.pdf.
Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bResidencyDocs (evidence pack).

If Horizen needs a signed attestation or SOC2 scan, we can provide the SOC2 summary and run an evidence call. Otherwise, we can prepare the export-control addendum if required.

— Karthik
